title: Visual review surface
description: Build Lite renders the whole RCF tree as a diagram and as a browsable static page, so a non-coding owner can see the documents and their links without reading any JSON. The view is read-only and generated from the on-disk tree on demand. Build/DAG sub-tab lays FBS by `dependsOnFbsIds` depth with click-to-highlight closure, dependency inspector, filters, unconnected lane and `#tab=build&sub=dag&entity=` deep links, per viewer UI refresh design section 7. ID lookup over a server-built `./index.json` of every document id and AC, opened by the SearchButton or Cmd/Ctrl+F, navigates to `#tab=<tab>&entity=<id>` preserving `embed` and `theme`, per viewer UI refresh design section 6. Embedding proof: a same-origin test-host fixture mounts the viewer with `embed=1` and `theme=` and the three lints keep framing headers, `target='_top'` and localStorage namespace in place, per viewer UI refresh design section 9 and Dex's wespa requirements of 2026-10-02. Standalone viewer carries a visible three-state theme control (Light|Dark|Auto) in the header right of the SearchButton that persists its setting under `rcf-view:v1:theme` in non-embed mode only (ADR-4137); under `embed=1` the control is absent from the DOM and the key is never read or written. Every text and control colour pair meets WCAG 2.1 AA (>= 4.5:1 for text, >= 3:1 for large text and non-text UI boundaries) in both themes, pinned by a static CSS-contrast audit test (US-207) that enumerates every rule and state in `src/view/style.css` and fails the suite on any below-threshold pair.
rationale: The owner cannot review code and will not read raw JSON. A visual surface is the only way they can see and steer what is being built in their name. It is delivered first (Phase 3) so every later phase has a review surface.
